Alex / procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we want to lock down the KMS/HSM handoff and secrets lifecycle for your private deployment (VPC + on-prem HSM gateway). Attached is a short provenance checklist and a network diagram that show the places keys and encrypted artifacts move in production. Key asks from our side so we can finalize the deployment runbook: 

- Confirm HSM model + interface: PKCS#11, KMIP, or both?
- Confirm whether FinSight will provide BYOK material (PEM/PKCS#12) or if you prefer Redwood to generate KEK and wrap it for escrow.
- Certificate chain and signer (do you require an offline root key ceremony and certs we should pin?).
- Rotation policy: suggest DEK rotation every 90 days, KEK (customer-managed) annual with a rollover window.
- Operator access: list of IPs for bastion and just-in-time access controls (we support ephemeral JIT via SSM or cloud IAM).
- Audit and retention: do you require NIST 800-53 mapping / audit log retention >1 year?

Next steps I'd like to propose: 1) confirm the HSM interface and cert owner, 2) hand off the exact certs to our security engineering (SFTP or Vault transit as you prefer), 3) schedule a short key-ceremony dry run. I copied Dylan + Mina to help with the technical runbook and audit attachments.

Attachments: provenance-checklist.xlsx, diagram-private-kms.png

Camila —

Thanks for the checklist. A few quick answers and a couple of clarifying questions: 

- HSM: We currently run an Azure Dedicated HSM appliance on-prem that supports PKCS#11 and a KMIP translation layer for legacy appliances. Prefer PKCS#11 for performance but we can expose KMIP if needed.
- BYOK: Procurement would prefer to hand over a wrapped KEK (customer-generated) rather than hand raw private key material. We can do an offline key ceremony and provide certs in PEM/DER.
- Certs: We need to ensure the signing cert chain is included; FinSight uses an internal root that's not publicly trusted — will Redwood accept a pinned CA cert?
- Rotation: Agreed to the suggested cadence, but we need a documented rollback if a KEK rollover fails (can't break access to historic ciphertext).
- Audit: We require audit records mapped to our SIEM for at least 18 months and SAML assertion correlation.

Question: Does Redwood support the ability to import HSM-wrapped keys (i.e., import a wrapped KEK and keep it non-exportable inside your runtime)? Also, what is your recommended approach for envelope encryption vs. relying solely on HSM-wrapped DEKs?

I can route certs and the procurement paperwork after we get confirmation on the import model.

—Alex Mercado
Security Engineering, FinSight
alex.mercado@finsight.com

Alex —

Short answers: yes on both PKCS#11 and KMIP; and yes, we support import of HSM-wrapped KEKs with non-exportability enforced by the runtime. A bit more detail below — pasted for provenance.

- Interfaces: Redwood runtime supports PKCS#11 natively and a KMIP proxy shim for teams that need protocol translation. For a high-traffic path (low-latency), PKCS#11 is preferred.

- Import model: We can accept a wrapped KEK (customer-wrapped with an HSM root key). The runtime stores the wrapped blob and uses the runtime HSM/KMS to unwrap into a volatile KEK held in memory (never written to disk). We sign the import transaction and persist an import audit record (non-repudiable).

- Envelope pattern: Recommended: keep data encrypted with ephemeral DEKs (fast, rotated frequently). DEKs are wrapped by the customer-managed KEK (BYOK) which stays non-exportable. This hybrid gives the best performance and allows fast rotation of DEKs without requiring high-latency HSM ops per token.

- Rollback: We'll maintain key versions and a transparent version table; if a KEK rollover fails we can mount prior KEK version to continue decrypting existing blobs — requires we get a copy of the previous wrapped key when the customer performs a rollover (standard practice).

- Ops and access: enforce operator access via a bastion + ephemeral certs (we can integrate with your SAML provider for JIT roles) and require HSM certs be delivered through an SFTP endpoint or via HashiCorp Vault transit with wrapped-transfer.

- Audit mapping: runtime emits structured events (JSON) to a push endpoint or S3; we can forward to an on-prem SIEM; retention configurable up to several years per agreement.

I'll draft a short action plan and a minimal runbook for the key ceremony — copying Mina who will own the runbook doc and the audit mapping.

Team / Alex —

Attached is a proposed action plan and the access matrix I referenced. Highlights: 

1) Pre-flight (week 0)
  - Confirm HSM interface (PKCS#11 preferred).
  - Mutual delivery of CA certs and pin list.
  - Procurement to deliver the wrapped KEK bundle to SFTP endpoint (instructions in attachment).

2) Dry run (week 1)
  - Perform import into a staging cluster; verify non-exportability and unseal flows.
  - Run decryption/rollback test vectors (we will provide test ciphertexts).

3) Production rollout (week 2)
  - Coordinate short maintenance window for KEK import and distribution across nodes.
  - Enable audit forwarding to your SIEM and verify retention policy.

Open decisions we need Alex to confirm: 
- Will FinSight supply both the wrapped KEK and the previous KEK (for immediate rollback)?
- Which delivery method do you prefer (SFTP vs. Vault transit)?
- Are there firewall egress rules we need to add to your bastion for runtime-to-HSM control channel (port 5696 / custom)?

Attachments: action-plan.md, kms-access-matrix.csv

Mina Haddad
Security Engineering

Alex —

Thanks for the fast turn. Based on the thread and the attached runbook, here are the agreed next steps and owners: 

- FinSight (Alex): provide the wrapped KEK bundle + previous wrapped KEK (for rollback) to our SFTP endpoint by Monday, Dec 14. Confirm CA cert bundle and preferred delivery method.
- Redwood (Mina): run the staging dry-run import (week of Dec 15) and share test vectors.
- Redwood (Dylan): validate PKCS#11 pinning and performance baseline; will produce a perf report after staging.
- Ops (Jonas): confirm firewall rules and bastion JIT ACLs; will send IP list for allowlist.

I scheduled a 30-minute follow-up to review the dry-run results and sign the deployment checklist: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=meet-abc123 

If those owners are correct, please confirm and we'll proceed. Once we receive the wrapped KEKs we will perform the import in staging and send a signed import manifest back for your records.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
